explanation: In C++, function objects (also known as functors) are objects that overload the function call operator 'operator()'. They enable encapsulating behavior within objects, allowing them to be used like functions. The standard library provides predefined function objects and adapters, such as std::mem_fun_ref, which adapt member functions into function objects that can be used with algorithms. This approach promotes flexible, reusable, and expressive code, especially when working with collections and algorithms in a modern C++ context.
syntax:
template <class T> std::mem_fun_ref<ReturnType (Class::*)()> mem_fun_ref(ReturnType (Class::*pm)());
// Usage with algorithms: std::for_each(collection.begin(), collection.end(), mem_fun_ref(&Class::memberFunction));
code_example: // Use std::mem_fun_ref to call save() on each Person in the collection
example_explanation: This example creates a vector of Person objects and uses std::for_each combined with std::mem_fun_ref to invoke the save() member function on each Person in the collection. It demonstrates how function objects, specifically std::mem_fun_ref, adapt member functions into callable objects compatible with algorithms, exemplifying modern C++'s functional programming capabilities and object-oriented design.
